capitals.name: Moche (Huacas del Sol y de la Luna)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Moche'; the text places the Southern Moche capital near present-day Moche, probably at the Huaca del Sol-Huaca de la Luna site (the Huaca de la Luna page: 'the ancient Moche capital city of Cerro Blanco'). Coordinates are the gazetteer's. Pampa Grande in the Lambayeque valley was prominent in Moche V (600-700) and San José de Moro in the Jequetepeque valley 400-850.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 100-799: the page gives no area for the culture; it names a Southern Moche heartland in the Chicama and Moche valleys and a Northern Moche polity in the lower Lambayeque (La Leche, Reque, Zaña) and lower Jequetepeque valley systems. Piura was 'fully part of the Moche phenomenon only for a short time' in Early Moche and is left out; influence reached Virú. The northern strip is drawn from 100 for want of dates.

ledger.note: c. 100: the Moche culture begins on the north coast of Peru. Infobox 'Established: 100 CE'; the culture 'flourished from about 100 to 800 AD' with Early (100-300), Middle (300-600) and Late (500-800) phases. The page calls it 'a group of autonomous polities that shared a common culture', not an empire.

ledger.note: c. 800: the Moche culture ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 800 CE'; Moche polities survived beyond 650 in the Jequetepeque and Moche valleys; a possible 'super El Niño' c. 563-594 and inter-elite quarrelling are named as causes, and the page finds 'no evidence' of a Huari invasion. Heirs: Sicán in the north, Chimú in the south (the Chimú appear about 900).

wars.name: Alleged Wari invasion of the Moche area
wars.outcome: The page says there is no evidence of a foreign invasion such as a Huari one; defensive works in the Jequetepeque valley point to unrest over scarce resources.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered; no territorial result.

notes: A culture, not a state: the page says the Moche were 'a group of autonomous polities that shared a common culture' and that centralised control 'may have taken place from time to time, but appears infrequent'. Cliopatria has no Moche row. Dates are the infobox's (100-800); the page also dates the Early Intermediate Period to 400 BC-600 AD (conflict). The Huaca de la Luna page gives 'inhabited between the 1st and 9th century AD' and no abandonment date. Chimor (900) leaves a century after 800 with no state on the Moche valley; the Sicán (750) overlaps the Moche north. Extents are the page's valley names read through the gazetteer, not boundaries. Capital coordinates are the gazetteer's for Moche.
